questions.question:
[지문]
It has been said that most people listen with the intention to reply rather than to understand. Your job as a mentor is to facilitate your mentee's thinking and not to try and do it for them, no matter how tempting that may be. If, during a mentoring session, you realise you're doing most of the talking, then I'd respectfully suggest that you just stop, sit back and listen. A good part of the mentee's learning process is happening when he/she thinks out loud. Therefore, your mentee should be doing most of the talking. Listening actively and empathically helps mentees to gain insight and to express themselves more effectively.

다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 멘토가 말을 적게 하고 듣기를 중시해야 하며, 멘티가 대부분 말하도록 해야 한다는 것입니다. 이는 '말을 적게 하고, 더 많이 들어라(Talk Less, Listen More)'라는 내용과 정확히 일치합니다.

options: Expert Knowledge: A Mandatory Key to Creativity

The Paradox of Expertise: When Knowledge Limits Creativity
How to Master a Field and Become an Expert
The Role of Constant Practice in Creative Thinking
questions.question:
[지문]
The expert myth is the belief that the more you know, the more creative you become. At the face of it, this seems quite logical. The rationale is that in order to be truly creative, one must master a field or a domain. Creativity often requires some level of expertise, but expertise and creativity are nonetheless very different things. Research into the lives of creative people shows that in some cases expertise can actually hinder the creative ability of individuals. As expertise grows, creativity sometimes diminishes. Sometimes the best insights come from those outside a particular field. There is good reason for this. When we are too heavily invested in a task, we may tend to overlook the obvious.

다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 전문성이 높을수록 창의성이 떨어질 수 있다는 역설(paradox)을 설명합니다. 처음에는 전문성이 창의성을 높인다고 생각하지만(the expert myth), 실제로는 전문성이 창의성을 방해할 수 있다는 모순을 다루므로 '전문성의 역설: 지식이 창의성을 제한할 때'가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Just as you don't know everything in advance about a trip you are going to take, neither can you know everything about how your new life or career might unfold. But that's fine. You just have to treat it like doing a jigsaw: accept that the full picture is going to emerge gradually rather than instantly. While sometimes it will be straightforward to fit pieces together, at other times it will take more effort and patience. Sometimes you will find interesting pieces that open up a whole new section, and at other times you may find pieces that don't seem to belong anywhere right now. You just need to keep at it until the picture emerges and you can see clearly what you have achieved.

How Cultural Diversity Enriches Our Daily Lives
questions.question:
[지문]
We don’t choose our earliest habits; we imitate them. We follow the script handed 
down by our friends and family, our church or school, our local community, and 
society at large. Each of these cultures and groups comes with its own set of 
expectations and standards — when and whether to get married, how many 
children to have, which holidays to celebrate, how much money to spend on your 
child’s birthday party. In many ways, these social norms are the invisible rules that guide your behavior each day. You’re always keeping them in mind, even if 
they are not at the top of your mind. Often, you follow the habits of your culture 
without thinking, without questioning, and sometimes without remembering. As the 
French philosopher Michel de Montaigne wrote, “The customs and practices of life 
in society sweep us along.”

questions.explanation: 우리가 습관을 직접 선택하기보다 사회적 규범과 관습이라는 '보이지 않는 대본'을 모 방하며 살아간다는 내용이므로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.

Nothing about an organization's strategy or business model is sacrosanct. But there must be a cutting point between principles and values and everything else. They represent precious, freestanding assets that must be independent of strategy. They provide continuity and identity when everything else is expendable. Cases in which leaders have successfully remodeled an entire enterprise represent organizational change in its comprehensive and supreme category. We learn from these cases that retaining principles and values during the process of change is not only possible but necessary to provide an anchor. Ironically, perhaps, organizations with the strongest principles and values often have the highest adaptive capacity because people attach themselves to them and understand that everything else is on the table. If you want to keep your promises, burn the house when it's time to reinvent the company. But save the nails.

다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 글의 주요 내용은 조직 변화 중에 핵심 원칙과 가치를 유지하는 것의 중요성이다. 전략이나 비즈니스 모델은 변할 수 있지만 원칙과 가치는 유지되어야 한다는 것을 강조한다. 이는 '근본적인 조직 변화 속에서 핵심 가치 보존'이라는 의미의 ③번이 가장 적절하다.

We learn from these cases that ④ <u>retain</u> principles and values during the process of change is not only possible but necessary to provide an anchor. If you want to keep your promises, ⑤ <u>burn</u> the house when it's time to reinvent the company. But save the nails.

questions.question:
[지문]
There is something in human nature that prompts us to think of our actions, as well as our feelings, as though they were the distinctive issue of something inside us, something uniquely ours. Some are. But most of the actions and feelings that help us enter into working relations with fellow members of the world are not all that private. They are, in fact, performances we execute in acceptably close conformity to widely accepted social rules. These rules are learned and held by us in such an easy way that we indulge the conceit that they are our own brilliant accomplishments. We think of them as though they were the inventions of our own utterly original psychic lives, when most of them are as familiar to others as they are to us. Social things are quite simply social.

다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 우리가 사회적 규칙에 따른 행동을 자신의 창의적 발명으로 착각한다는 것이다. 문장 'We think of them as though they were the inventions of our own utterly original psychic lives, when most of them are as familiar to others'가 이를 명확히 보여준다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Cooked food does many familiar things. It makes our food safer and creates delicious tastes. However, the most critical advantage is that cooking increases the amount of energy we can get from food. This extra energy gave the first cooks biological advantages, allowing them to survive and reproduce better. Over time, human bodies adapted to this new diet through natural selection, leading to significant changes in anatomy, physiology, and even society. Fossil evidence suggests that this dependence on cooked food began at the very start of human evolution. We should indeed pin our humanity on cooks.

다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 요리가 인류의 진화와 생물학적 변화에 어떤 영향을 미쳤는지를 설명하는 것이다. 'biological advantages', 'adapted through natural selection', 'significant changes in anatomy, physiology' 등의 표현이 이를 보여준다.

ago, but right back at the beginning of our time on Earth.

questions.explanation: 'indicates' 뒤의 'that' 절 안에서 주어는 'this dependence'이며, 이에 대응하는 본 동사가 필요합니다. 문맥상 과거에 일어난 일이므로 과거동사 'arose'가 적절합니다.

( ③ ) They survived and reproduced better than before, and their genes spread. ( ④ ) Their bodies responded by biologically adapting to cooked food, shaped by natural selection to take maximum advantage of the new diet. ( ⑤ ) Fossil evidence indicates that this dependence arose at the start of human evolution.
